The graph of the linear function $g$ is shown, where $y = g(x)$. What is the x-intercept of the graph of $g$?
explanation: Choice C is correct. The x-intercept of a graph is the point where the graph intersects the x-axis. The graph of function $g$, where $y = g(x)$, intersects the x-axis at $(6, 0)$. Therefore, the x-intercept of the graph of $g$ is $(6, 0)$.
